originality.rationale: Prior work contains the full one-dimensional gamma-to-Gaussian eigenvalue approximation and the single-frequency radial counterexample; these are explicitly excluded from novelty. The assembled result proves the exact spectrum and Berezin cluster intervals simultaneously for every continuous real periodic radial profile in all fixed complex dimensions, determines precisely when an offset yields a false-positive test, and establishes a globally sharp Lipschitz bound with a periodic tent extremizing sequence. Source comparisons and targeted mathematical-record searches did not reveal these combined all-periodic and sharp quantitative statements. Residual risk: an unstated elementary combination of known heat-kernel formulas might already imply part of the classification.
residual_risks: The spectral half follows directly from an existing all-symbol smoothing theorem in one dimension, so broad novelty belongs to the paired profile classification, exact offset threshold and sharp Lipschitz envelope, not the heat kernels themselves.
An unlocated general result combining radial Toeplitz eigenvalue asymptotics with asymptotic coherent-state averaging could imply the two-range formula; search absence is not a proof of priority.

The Lipschitz coefficient uses standard Gaussian coupling; its contribution is the exact global operator-theoretic gap supremum with a periodic extremizing family, not invention of a transport inequality.

value.rationale: The original research question asks when positive Berezin liminf falsely diagnoses essential positivity. The result provides a complete and directly usable phase classification for all nonconstant continuous periodic radial profiles, exact spectral and Berezin intervals independent of dimension, and the best possible Lipschitz-normalized width of the discrepancy; arbitrary two-frequency profiles illustrate nontrivial interference absent from one-cosine models. Both classification and sharp global quantitative envelope are structurally motivated, not arbitrary parameter substitutions. The general one-dimensional heat spectral ingredient and older cosine special cases are fully credited.
